data.title: YAML engine leverages ISB-provided S3 read and write
data.goal: ISB gives collectors access to write into the S3 storage URL provided by the backend. Some native collectors already use it to stay stable against an ever-moving asset inventory. Bring that capability to the yaml-adapter-engine so YAML adapters can read from and write to that S3 location. Research into how the existing collectors use it follows task open.

lesson.statement: In yaml-adapter-engine aabc8cf, pagination.expected_total_path asserts completeness only when a cursor walk ends by natural exhaustion, not at a max_pages cap; so it does not turn the Axonius bundle's max_pages 500 x limit 2000 truncation into a failure.
lesson.doNot: rely on pagination.expected_total_path to catch a walk that stopped at max_pages; the completeness check skips a max_pages stop, so set max_pages far above any tenant

lesson.statement: The Axonius get_devices cursor strategy reads meta.next_page only when it is a JSON string; any other JSON type ends the walk after page 1 with a success result.
lesson.doNot: assume a cursor pagination walk continues when the vendor cursor is not a JSON string; the engine stops after page one with success, so pair cursor strategy with expected_total_path

constraint.statement: Source of truth: IntegrationServiceBus, IntegrationInfra and cymulate-integration-adapters at origin/dev (local checkouts are on dev and pulled). yaml-adapter-engine: read master and compare with dev, because production runs master. Uncommitted working-tree changes are not source of truth.

Map what FalconCollector and TenableIoCollector do today with the ISB-provided S3 storage (storageUrl): the technique, the seams, and the result. ISB side: Infrastructure.AWS/Services. Access layer: IntegrationInfra.
The yaml-adapter-engine must support the same capability, declared in the YAML, opt-in, composed on demand from the YAML. Integrations that do not declare it must behave exactly as today.
This phase maps, understands and provides the technical capability. Flexibility and integration-specific use come later. Falcon is the pilot integration.

Deliverable of this phase: a complete InternalRecon and a PromptContract, filed as artifacts. The coordinator stops at the handoff to the orchestrator; a fresh orchestrator agent receives the task path and writes the OrchestrationPlan. No code changes in target repositories during this phase.
Identifier prefixes: operator C/E/D/K/ALT; recon run (s3-storage-recon) RC/RE/RD/RALT; contract designer (s3-contract-designer) PC/PE/PD/PALT.

claim.statement: FalconCollector and TenableIoCollector use the ISB-provided S3 storage through IntegrationInfra (IAdapterObjectStore, GuardedObjectStore, BatchScopedStorage, PriorStateStore, StagingManifest) to keep state across pages and runs, and this is what makes their results stable against a changing asset inventory.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If they use a different path or the stability comes from elsewhere, the seam map and the YAML design target the wrong mechanism.

claim.statement: The yaml-adapter-engine has no access to the S3 object store today; it reaches IntegrationInfra only through the host that runs it (YamlCollector in cymulate-integration-adapters).
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If true, the capability needs a host pass-through and a second-repo release, not only a YAML keyword.

claim.statement: The capability can be declared as an opt-in YAML construct without changing behaviour or output identity for integrations that do not declare it.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If not, every existing YAML integration changes on the engine upgrade.

claim.statement: The Falcon YAML integration in integration-yaml is a usable pilot: it runs on the engine today and its native counterpart FalconCollector uses the S3 storage.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If not, the pilot must change before the plan can name its verification.

claim.statement: Native FalconCollector findings is two-phase and requires the ISB object store: it resolves IAdapterObjectStore (and optional IAdapterObjectPruner) from IAdapterExecutionContext.Services, wraps it in IntegrationInfra GuardedObjectStore, spools Discover host pages to {storageUrl}/_staging/gen_<ticks>/hosts_NNNNNN.json plus manifest.json (Phase 1, no enrichment), then walks that frozen aid list in AidBatchSize batches for Spotlight (Phase 2). A missing store or storageUrl fails the run. It uses its own FalconFrozenKeyList, not IntegrationInfra FrozenKeyList.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If wrong, the YAML design would copy the wrong staging layout or resume authority.

claim.statement: Native TenableIoCollector correlated findings stages one object per asset at {storageUrl}/_staging/spine/<assetId>.json, one claim marker per published vulnerability chunk at _staging/claims/<chunkId>.ids, and a spine manifest written through IntegrationInfra StagingManifest. Its purpose is a bounded heap and resume-safe correlation of two independently snapshotted exports (assets and vulns), not freezing a mutable scroll. The object store is required; the pruner is optional and deletion is garbage collection.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If wrong, Tenable-style keyed lookup would be mis-modelled as the same technique as Falcon.

claim.statement: In cymulate-integration-adapters, IntegrationInfra FrozenKeyList and PriorStateStore have zero references; StagingManifest is referenced only by TenableIoAssetSpine; GuardedObjectStore is used by both Falcon and Tenable.io.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If wrong, a YAML design could rely on a primitive that no collector has exercised in production.

claim.statement: Falcon's stability against a moving asset inventory comes from the two-phase freeze (page the mutable-ordered scroll and write keys only, freeze the list, then enrich by walking the frozen list), not from S3 storage as such. S3 is the durable place the frozen list and staged pages live across legs and pods.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If wrong, adding read/write alone to the engine would not remove the replay defect.

claim.statement: The YAML engine's host in production is the YamlAdapter project in cymulate-integration-adapters (Collectors/YamlCollector is not tracked at origin/dev). YamlAdapter does not resolve IAdapterObjectStore today, but it can: ISB AdapterExecutionContext.Services is the ISB host service provider, and ISB registers S3ObjectStore as IAdapterObjectStore whenever a data bucket is configured (pruner only when ObjectPruningEnabled).
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If wrong, the host pass-through needs an ISB change as well as an adapters change.

claim.statement: The yaml-adapter-engine has no Cymulate.* package dependency by rule, and host concerns cross into it only through engine-owned interfaces implemented by the host (IWorkflowHost, IExecutionSink, IResumeStateSink). An object-store capability must therefore be an engine-owned port that YamlAdapter implements over IAdapterObjectStore behind GuardedObjectStore.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If wrong, the engine could take a direct dependency, which its CLAUDE.md rule 0 rejects on sight.

claim.statement: The Falcon YAML pilot on integration-yaml master (72a99e2) runs Spotlight merge_into enrichment per page inside the Discover scroll query_hosts_for_findings, which filters last_seen_timestamp:>= and sorts last_seen_timestamp.asc. This is the single-phase shape the native design doc names as the cause of the measured 29.2% asset replay. Its declared parity target is native FalconCollector v5.0.0, which predates the two-phase flow.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If wrong, the pilot would not demonstrate the capability's benefit.

claim.statement: The engine already expresses a two-phase shape in memory: a stage with collect: accumulates distinct record values in first-appearance order, a later for_each stage walks {{stages.<name>.collected.<key>}} one element per operation instance, and resume uses the positional ForEachIndex. The collected list persists only inside WorkflowCheckpoint.StagesOutputJson, which the host writes into the ISB checkpoint row on every page and item.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If wrong, the S3-backed design would duplicate or contradict an existing engine mechanism.

claim.statement: The engine's integration schema is closed (additionalProperties false at the document root, on flowStep, on the workflow stage item and on mergeInto) and the collector path validates against it. A new YAML key needs an engine schema change and an engine release before any definition can carry it; a definition that does not carry the key is unaffected by the schema change.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If wrong, either old definitions break on upgrade or a new key is silently ignored.

claim.statement: Proceeding on unverified: adding any property to the engine's StepPlan record changes PlanDigest for every compiled plan, including plans that never use the new capability, because PlanDigest serializes with default options that write null properties. A pinned plan digested by an older engine would then fail the digest check in YamlAdapter PinnedPlanReader and fall back to compiling the YAML, logged at Error as DigestMismatch.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If true and unhandled, integrations that do not declare the capability change observable behaviour (pinned-plan fallback), which violates K3.

claim.statement: IntegrationInfra origin/dev (b2791a0, 2026-08-16, Version 1.2.0-preview.0) is not the source of the IntegrationInfra package the adapters consume (origin/dev pins Cymulate.IntegrationInfra 1.8.0-preview.0; the newest Infra line is origin/refactor/appcore-namespaces 6ea544f at 1.10.0-preview.0). The object-store surface (IAdapterObjectStore, ObjectStoreRequests, ObjectStoreExceptions, IAdapterExecutionContext, Ingestion/, BatchScopedStorage) has no diff between origin/dev and origin/refactor/appcore-namespaces.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If the surface had diverged, K1's source of truth for IntegrationInfra would describe a contract nobody runs.

claim.statement: cymulate-integration-adapters origin/dev pins Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine 1.0.0-preview.29. yaml-adapter-engine origin/master (aabc8cf) is 7 commits behind origin/dev (fa10015) and 0 ahead; none of the 23 differing files is a host-seam file (IWorkflowHost, IExecutionSink, IResumeStateSink, StageConfig, CollectConfig, WorkflowCheckpoint, FanOutStageRunner, SinkRoutedStageRunner, StepPlan, PlanJson, PlanDigest).
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If wrong, a seam described from dev would not exist on the master production runs.

claim.statement: YAML egress (YamlAdapter WorkflowPublishSink over IntegrationInfra NdjsonBatchEmitter) publishes assets_*/findings_* objects at the run root of storageUrl. Anything the capability stages under storageUrl must live under a leading-underscore segment such as _staging, because the parser selects input by an undelimited string-prefix match on assets/findings.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If ignored, staged control artifacts are ingested as customer data.

alternative.statement: Give the yaml-adapter-engine direct object-store access by referencing Cymulate.Integration.Client (IAdapterObjectStore) or AWSSDK.S3 from the engine project.
alternative.rejectionRationale: Engine CLAUDE.md rule 0 rejects any Cymulate.* reference on sight (it is what keeps the engine packageable), and the design of record forbids collectors from constructing cloud clients. The engine must own a storage port and the host must implement it (RC6, RE6).

alternative.statement: Implement the host side of the capability with the AWSSDK.S3 client YamlAdapter already carries for S3YamlDefinitionLoader, instead of resolving IAdapterObjectStore from IAdapterExecutionContext.Services.
alternative.rejectionRationale: It would bypass ISB's storageUrl-to-bucket/key resolution, its 403-versus-404 resume rule and multipart handling in S3ObjectStore, and IntegrationInfra GuardedObjectStore read limits, which both native collectors go through (RC1, RC2, RC5). The design of record states collectors reach storage only through the Infra facade.

newLessons.statement: device_policies.prevention.settings_hash exists and is populated on Falcon device entities.
newLessons.outcome: No live vendor response was inspected. The landed edge carries the vendor assignment object verbatim, so the field is neither extracted nor asserted -- exactly as unverified as at baseRef. Not vendor-documented; searched official CrowdStrike docs and FalconPy source and found nothing.
newLessons.doNot: Do not treat a downstream parser reading a vendor field as proof the vendor populates it.

newLessons.statement: Emission order does not affect identity for the staged policy plane artifacts.
newLessons.outcome: No test asserts ordering determinism. Both artifacts are serialized from Dictionary enumerations with no contractual order; the risk is structurally avoided because both are read back id-keyed and neither is published, which is an argument rather than evidence.
newLessons.doNot: Do not conflate unstable ordering with unstable identity, and do not rely on Dictionary enumeration order for a persisted artifact.

newLessons.statement: AidExtractor.ExtractAid can derive a unique key for a Discover asset that states no sensor AID.
newLessons.outcome: Live full-inventory probe of 303 lab assets: 49 state an AID and the derivation produced a key for 0 of the remaining 254. The 32-hex suffix gate rejects the tenant's 56-char base64url token.
newLessons.doNot: do not re-assume a derived AID keys an unmanaged Discover entity without probing that tenant's combined id shape first

newLessons.statement: The Falcon checkpoint's boundary-key list has a ceiling that fails visibly if it grows.
newLessons.outcome: The collector imposes no cap on that path and neither AdapterCheckpoint.AdapterState nor CommitPage documents one. Measured 460,022 bytes at a full 5,000-key set; it is pinned by a test, not capped.
newLessons.doNot: do not assume a control artifact carrying a growable list is bounded because a sibling artifact is

newLessons.statement: The Discover cursor leg observes a Falcon 404 as an HTTP 404 status line, so its re-anchor arm fires on an expired cursor.
newLessons.outcome: No probe of the 404-under-200 behaviour was run in this task and the changed cursor leg was never exercised against one, so the re-anchor arm remains unproven on the code path this task edited. Four neighbouring beliefs stayed untested for a stated reason rather than an unexamined one: remediation-entity ordering is moot because the fallback key is the combined id verbatim, settings_hash is unreachable while prevention enrichment ships off, and device-entities batch membership is unchanged because it derives from the sensor AID, which is null for every AID-less host.
newLessons.doNot: do not read an absent re-anchor count as evidence the cursor never expired; the vendor can deliver 404 under a 200 header

newLessons.statement: Falcon findings never arrive without a matching asset in the same collection batch.
newLessons.outcome: Zero orphans holds only at the default 2000-01-01 floor. The assets lane gates on last_seen_timestamp and the findings lane on updated_timestamp against the same floor, so a host not seen recently leaves the asset lane while its findings still pass: 3,342 orphans across 8 keys measured at --base-date 2026-08-30.
newLessons.doNot: do not assume two independently-gated vendor lanes are mutually consistent without checking which vendor clock each one filters on

newLessons.statement: A ~300 host and ~100k finding lab collection is short enough to re-run repeatedly during development.
newLessons.outcome: Exactly one 236.2 s run exists and it was not repeated: it needs live credentials and would overwrite the batch the suite pins by name, and each run writes a 496 MB findings file.
newLessons.doNot: do not plan an iteration loop around re-collecting from a live tenant when the suite pins a single batch by name

newLessons.statement: Build the bundle on Axonius REST API v1 (POST /api/devices, JSON:API body)
newLessons.outcome: Operator 2026-09-23: v1 is deprecated (axonius-api-client 5.0.22 is bug-fix only, AC8), so it is not used; v2 is the target (K8).
newLessons.verify: none — vendor lifecycle facts come from Axonius web pages, not a repository
newLessons.doNot: report 'Axonius API v1 is deprecated'; what is deprecated is the v1 Python client (axonius-api-client); the v1 REST API is still served with no published end-of-life, and v2 is recommended

claim.statement: Proceeding on unverified: a key list carried in YAML workflow checkpoint state (collect: values inside WorkflowCheckpoint.StagesOutputJson) has no size ceiling in the engine, YamlAdapter or ISB checkpoint path, so a Falcon-scale collected aid list grows the checkpoint blob without a visible failure.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If true, keeping the frozen key list in checkpoint state instead of the object store is unbounded, which is an argument for the S3-backed list.

claim.statement: Proceeding on unverified: a YAML Phase-1 spool that ends at pagination.max_pages is not detected as incomplete by expected_total_path (engine aabc8cf PaginationConfig.cs:171-183), so a freeze built on such a walk could persist a truncated frozen key list as if complete.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If true and unguarded, a frozen list would silently omit hosts on every resumed leg, because a frozen list is reused rather than re-derived.

claim.statement: Proceeding on unverified: a staged key list the engine persists has a contractual, deterministic order (for example first-appearance order from the spool) and does not depend on Dictionary or HashSet enumeration order.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If wrong, batch k covers different keys on different legs, which is the exact failure a frozen positional list exists to prevent.

### FalconCollector — technique: two-phase freeze (`key_driven_probe`) — RC1, RC4

| step | what happens | code |
|---|---|---|
| bind | `IAdapterObjectStore` (+ optional `IAdapterObjectPruner`) from `IAdapterExecutionContext.Services`, wrapped in `GuardedObjectStore`; missing store or `storageUrl` **fails the run** (no silent fallback) | `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:758-791` |

| freeze | a completed generation is **reused, never re-derived**; a progressed checkpoint whose generation is gone fails | `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:578-598` |
| Phase 2 | walk the frozen aid list (`FalconFrozenKeyList.EnumerateAsync`) in `AidBatchSize` batches; one aid-scoped Spotlight scroll per batch; publish one object per batch through `NdjsonBatchEmitter` | `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:288-379` |
| resume | position is (staged page, batch index) inside one generation; object name = host page counter | `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:175-199,311-322` |
| cleanup | never deletes a completed generation (checkpoint write has no durable ack); run-scoped lifecycle reclaims | `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:376-418` |

**Result:** stability comes from the freeze, not from storage (RC4). S3 is where the frozen list and
the staged pages survive across legs and pods.

### TenableIoCollector — technique: keyed asset spine (`grouped_probe`-like) — RC2

- Spool `/assets/export` to `_staging/spine/<assetId>.json` (one object per asset, identity key, so a
  re-spool converges); spine manifest through Infra `StagingManifest`.
- Stream `/vulns/export` chunks; look each asset up by key (`TryReadAsync` → null = miss).
- Claim marker per published chunk `_staging/claims/<chunkId>.ids`, written **before** the data object.
- Sweep assets no chunk claimed as empty-findings envelopes; delete spine if a pruner exists.
- Purpose: bounded heap and resume-safe correlation of two independently snapshotted exports. Not a
  mutable-scroll freeze.
- Code: `TenableIoAssetSpine.cs:13-404`, `TenableIoSpinePaths.cs:5-74`, `TenableIoCorrelatedFindingsFlow.cs:14-335`.

- Host port with default members → `IWorkflowHost.cs:72,79` (`StepStarted`/`StepCompleted` default

- Resolve storage from DI, never construct a client; fail hard when required and absent →

- Always go through `GuardedObjectStore` with `IngestionOptions.Resolve` / `MemoryPressureOptions.Resolve`
  → `TenableIoCorrelatedFindingsFlow.cs:326-330`.
- Base URL from `BatchScopedStorage.ResolveBaseUrl`, never re-implemented → `BatchScopedStorage.cs:207-218`.
- Staged paths under `_staging/`, asserted at run start → `FalconStagingPaths.cs:120-156`.
- Write-once frozen list; completion proved by a manifest written last; reuse, never re-derive →
  `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:557-628`; design doc section 5.
- Deterministic keys from identity or geometry, never a counter → design doc section 6.
- Checkpoint: `SetState` before `AdvancePage` → `StageCheckpointWriter.cs:9-16`.
- Opt-in by absence: a stage feature exists only when its key is present (e.g. `merge_into`, `collect`,
  `poll` are nullable on `StageConfig`/`StepPlan`).

## Existing engine mechanism the design must extend, not duplicate — RC8, RC14

- `collect:` on a stage accumulates distinct values in first-appearance order
  (`StageCollections.cs:7-62`); a later `for_each: "{{stages.X.collected.k}}"` stage runs once per
  element (`FanOutStageRunner.cs:23-58,114-133`); resume is positional (`ForEachIndex`).
- That **is** a two-phase freeze — but the list lives only in heap and in `WorkflowCheckpoint.StagesOutputJson`,
  re-serialized into the ISB checkpoint row on every page and item (`StageCheckpointWriter.cs:47-61`).
- Lesson L-35b88c57 (applied as RC14, OPEN): nothing caps that blob; a native sibling measured 460,022
  bytes for 5,000 keys. The S3-backed list is the bounded alternative.
- `for_each` runs one operation per element; Falcon needs one call per **batch** of keys
  (`aid:[…]`, 50 native / 250 YAML). Batching over a frozen list does not exist in `for_each` today
  (read of `FanOutStageRunner.ResolveItems`; not exhaustively searched for a chunking transform).

## The pilot today — RC7, C4

- `integration-yaml` master Falcon `collect` flow: `hosts` stage scrolls Discover
  (`filter last_seen_timestamp:>=`, `sort last_seen_timestamp.asc`, page 250, prefetch) and the
  `findings` stage is `merge_into: target: hosts` — Spotlight enrichment **per page inside the scroll**
  (`SinkRoutedStageRunner.cs:5-17`, `MergeEnrichmentSink.cs:13-22`).
- That is exactly the shape the design of record measured at 29.2% replay. Parity target is native
  v5.0.0, which predates two-phase.
- C4 stays OPEN: the definition uses only supported constructs and its native counterpart uses S3
  (RE14), but no deployment record was read, so "runs in production today" is not established.

## Shared surface to freeze

- **Engine storage port** (new, engine-owned, public): the minimal read/write/stat/list the engine needs
  over a run-scoped relative path, with absence as a value. Produced by engine work; consumed by the
  YamlAdapter host. Shape is a design decision for the contract/plan, not settled here.
- **How the host exposes it**: a new member on `IWorkflowHost` with a default body, or a separate
  interface the host may also implement (the `IResumeStateSink` precedent). Decide once, before either
  side starts.
- **YAML vocabulary**: key name(s), where they attach (flow step and legacy workflow stage are two
  separate schema copies — `flowStep` 1945-2042 and stage item 1569-1657), validation rules.
- **Staged layout contract**: `_staging/<something>/…`, manifest-last, deterministic order (RC16).
- **StepPlan field(s)** and their digest behaviour when absent (L3).

## Disjoint sets available

- `engine`: `yaml-adapter-engine/src/**` + `tests/**` — independent of `host` once the port is frozen.
- `host`: `cymulate-integration-adapters/src/Cymulate.Integration.Adapters/YamlAdapter/**` + its test
  project + `Directory.Packages.props` pin — depends on a **published** engine package carrying the port.
- `pilot`: `integration-yaml/integrations/crowdstrike-falcon/**` — depends on an engine release and an
  adapters release; K4 puts integration-specific use later.
- Split is by repository, so the multi-repo hard trigger applies. Engine tests and engine src are
  separable within `engine`.

## Landmines

- **L1 — IntegrationInfra origin/dev is not what runs.** Adapters pin `Cymulate.IntegrationInfra
  1.8.0-preview.0`; Infra origin/dev is `1.2.0-preview.0` (2026-08-16); newest line is
  `origin/refactor/appcore-namespaces` `1.10.0-preview.0`. The object-store surface is byte-identical
  across them (RC11), so this does not change the design — but no one should "fix" Infra dev as part
  of this task. Remote fetch was denied by the sandbox; refs are as last fetched.
- **L2 — The schema is closed.** `additionalProperties: false` at root (line 7), workflow (1560), stage
  item (1571), mergeInto (1700), flowStep (1947). A new key needs an engine release before any
  definition can carry it, and a definition carrying it fails `INVALID_PAYLOAD` on an older engine pin.
  Two schema copies (flowStep and workflow stage) must both change or the key works on one authoring
  surface only. Definitions deployed to S3 drift per environment (`YamlEngineFactory.cs:23-30`).
- **L3 — Plan digest changes for everyone.** `PlanDigest` serializes nulls, so any new `StepPlan`
  property changes every plan's digest; a pinned plan digested by an older engine then falls back with
  `DigestMismatch` logged at Error for integrations that never declared the capability — a K3
  violation unless the new property is omitted when absent (RC10, OPEN, needs a test). The plan
  producer is outside ISB (no `PlanDigest` reference there).
- **L4 — Parser visibility.** YAML egress writes `assets_*`/`findings_*` at the run root. Staged
  objects must sit under a leading-underscore segment (RC13); mirror the native run-start assertion.
- **L5 — Read-slot deadlock.** `GuardedObjectStore` enumerators (`ListAsync`, NDJSON reads) take no
  slot by design; a host adapter that wraps them must not hold a slot across a `yield` into engine code
  (Infra doc rule 2). At `MaxConcurrentReads: 1` it deadlocks.
- **L6 — Unknown-length writes.** A streamed staged list must reach S3 through multipart; ISB
  `S3ObjectStore` already does this for non-seekable streams. A host that buffers instead gives up the
  bounded-memory property.
- **L7 — IAM.** `s3:ListBucket` is required or `StatAsync` throws access-denied rather than returning
  absent. Deployment-time, not checkable from here.
- **L8 — Resume authority.** Falcon refuses to derive a second "where are we" from storage; the
  checkpoint is the only position authority and a manifest proves only completion. The YAML design
  must keep one authority (the `WorkflowCheckpoint`) and treat the manifest as a completion proof.
- **L9 — Truncated freeze.** `expected_total_path` does not fire on a `max_pages` stop (lesson GC1,
  applied as RC15, OPEN). A freeze over a capped walk would persist a short list as complete and every
  later leg reuses it.
- **L10 — Deterministic order.** Batch k must cover the same keys on every leg; the persisted list's
  order must be contractual, never a `Dictionary`/`HashSet` enumeration (lesson L-1a37307e, RC16, OPEN).
- **L11 — Local YamlCollector remnants.** `Collectors/YamlCollector/Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine`
  exists only as untracked build output locally; it is a vendored engine copy that must never load
  beside YamlAdapter (adapters CLAUDE.md). Ignore it.
- **L12 — Design-of-record tension.** The design doc deferred a YAML descriptor on purpose ("a second
  declarative interpreter beside the existing engine is a known trap"). This task adds the capability to
  the existing engine rather than a second interpreter, which is consistent with that warning, but the
  contract should say so.

## Lesson applicability

| lesson | decision | reason |
|---|---|---|
| L-35b88c57 (checkpoint key list has no ceiling) | applied → RC14 | the engine's existing collect/for_each keeps the list in checkpoint state |
| GC1 (expected_total_path skips max_pages stop) | applied → RC15 | a freeze must be provably complete |
| L-1a37307e (do not rely on Dictionary order for a persisted artifact) | applied → RC16 | positional frozen list |
| GC2 (cursor must be a JSON string) | not applied | Falcon `meta.pagination.after` is a string; not a storage concern |
| L-76ed5c8b (404 under 200 on cursor expiry) | not applied | Phase-1 scroll recovery, pilot-specific; K4 defers pilot use |
| L-29828585 (AID derivation for unmanaged hosts) | not applied | pilot key extraction, not the storage capability |
| L-cc8f607b (two lanes on different vendor clocks) | not applied | pilot correlation semantics, later phase |
| L-f88b5876 (lab re-collection cost) | not applied as a claim; noted for verification planning | live Falcon runs are expensive and not repeatable at will |
| L-00f62476 (settings_hash presence) | not applied | vendor field, unrelated |
| ALT2 Axonius v1 | not applied | unrelated vendor |

## Claims and disposition

| claim | status | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | rejected | RE3 |
| C2 | rejected | RE5 |
| C3 | open (structurally supported by RE9; blocked on L3) | RE9 |
| C4 | open (production dispatch not established) | RE14 |
| RC1–RC9, RC11–RC13 | validated | RE1–RE9, RE11–RE13 |
| RC10 | open — needs a test | RE10 |
| RC14–RC16 | open — lesson-derived | — |

Discarded approaches: RALT1 (engine references Client/AWSSDK), RALT2 (host uses YamlAdapter's own
AWSSDK.S3 client).

## What recon leaves to the contract and plan

- Whether the capability is (a) a generic staged read/write port only, or (b) the port plus a declared
  "freeze-then-walk" topology over it (Falcon's shape). K2/K3/K4 read as (b) for Falcon being the pilot;
  confirm in the contract.
- Whether batching over a frozen list is new engine vocabulary or an extension of `for_each`.
- Release order: engine publish → adapters pin bump + host port → definition change.
"

# User request (operator's words, verbatim)

## Task name
please create a governed task thusly named: yaml-engine-to-leverage-s3-read-and-right
(id corrected by the operator to "read-and-write")

## Goal
ISB provides access to collectors to write into S3's storeage URL provided by the BE. this capability is used by some of the collectors already to achieve stability againts an ever moving asset inventory, research into that will be done after the task is opened

## Premise
- 1 -
a while back I added a capability for collectors to use S3/storageUrl as a cloud disk for collectors, this can be seen here
/Users/user/Dev/IntegrationServiceBus/src/Cymulate.IntegrationServiceBus/Infrastructure/Cymulate.IntegrationServiceBus.Infrastructure.AWS/Services

- 2 -
the access into this capability will have to be found here:
/Users/user/Dev/IntegrationInfra

- 3 -
the implementation is best seen with these two collectors:
/Users/user/Dev/cymulate-integration-adapters/src/Cymulate.Integration.Adapters/Collectors/FalconCollector
/Users/user/Dev/cymulate-integration-adapters/src/Cymulate.Integration.Adapters/Collectors/TenableIoCollector

- 4 -
A. we need to identify the technique, the seams, and the result
B. as the stated purpose, the yamle adapter engine should also be able to support this capability, described within the yaml in the same way
C. this should allow us to give any integration running on the yaml infrastructure a way to use S3's endless memory for stable results
D. this will be an opt in mechanism, of course, composed on demand from the yaml
E. the current concern is to map, understand and provide the technical capability - the flexibility and specific implementation will come after

- 5 -
your goal is to create a completed documentation, and a plan, which I will then hand off to a fresh agent for execution.
you are allowed to ask questions, name concerns and point to limitations to be covered if necessary

## Answers to the coordinator's questions
1. you may put ISB on dev and pull origin
2. what the current falcon and tenable do
3. falcon is the pilot
4. the fresh agent will get the path to the task, then I do my thing
5. the recon is internal, over existing code, not complecated. you are to follow what the coordinator is to do before it hand off the task to the orchestrator

## Direction on the capability's shape
how about a shapless option C?
we open up a door, use the storage url like collectors do, then allow nesting, then allow read and write
this, chained properly should allow similar freezing like falcon does now?

C with guardrails, but _staging as a fixed concept seems intrusive, no?
(accepted: the author names paths freely; the engine enforces only that the first segment starts with "_")

decision.statement: The capability is option C: open access to the ISB storage URL from the YAML engine through a host-implemented, engine-owned port; nested paths; read and write; opt-in and composed from the YAML. No fixed topology. Four guarantees are built into the primitives: (1) parser-invisible paths: the first segment of every declared storage path starts with '_', the name is chosen by the author, and load-time validation refuses otherwise; (2) complete-or-absent sets: a set's manifest is written last, reads and existence checks see only complete sets, and a walk ended by max_pages never completes a set; (3) a stage condition on the existence of a complete set; (4) batched, paged iteration over a stored set with positional resume in the WorkflowCheckpoint.
decision.rationale: Operator direction 2026-09-27. Recon RC4: stability comes from the freeze, not from storage; C lets the freeze be composed while K4 keeps flexibility for later. The guarantees move the correctness properties Falcon relies on (RC15, RC16, RC13, L8) into the engine so an author cannot silently lose them.

alternative.statement: Option B: a fixed declared freeze-then-walk topology (Falcon's shape) as one engine construct
alternative.rejectionRationale: Operator chose C: B fixes one shape, while K4 asks for the capability without a fixed shape; C with guarantees can compose the same freeze and also a Tenable-style keyed spine.

alternative.statement: A fixed reserved '_staging' folder, or a hidden prefix the engine adds to every path
alternative.rejectionRationale: Operator found a fixed name intrusive. The real invariant (RC13) is only that no staged object matches the parser's undelimited assets/findings prefix; a first-segment '_' rule enforces that without reserving a name, and a hidden prefix makes the YAML path differ from the S3 path.

constraint.statement: Contract success test: Falcon's current two-phase freeze, written as YAML using only the D1 primitives, as a worked example validated against the engine's schema and plan compiler design (not deployed; K4). If it cannot be written, the contract says so and names the missing primitive. The contract also states how integrations that do not opt in stay byte-identical, including plan digest (RC10/L3).

Before the contract-designer run stops: if its claim changes made RECON1 stale, it refreshes the recon from the same run (artifact recon-template, lesson consult --purpose recon, artifact record --kind InternalRecon --supersedes the current recon). Design to Scope is refused on a stale recon.

claim.statement: Proceeding on unverified: the storageUrl run root (stg/raw-data/{clientId}/{settingId}/{instanceId}) is unique to one collection run and shared by all resume legs of that run, so a stored set at a fixed author-chosen path is never visible to a later run. Only GenerateStoragePrefix (IntegrationInfra Client/Contracts/IAdapterExecutionContext.cs:378-399) was read; the backend that mints instanceId was not.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If instanceId is reused across runs, stored_absent skips Phase 1 on every later run and the frozen set from the first run is reused forever: a stale inventory published as current. The design would then need a per-run generation token recorded in the WorkflowCheckpoint, which is a missing primitive.

claim.statement: Proceeding on unverified: a step whose records come from a stored set (from_store) can be a merge_into target, reusing the existing enrichment sink, and its positional resume can be carried by the existing WorkflowCheckpoint fields InTargetStage and TargetPage (next part index) with no new checkpoint property (engine Workflow/Contracts/Models/WorkflowCheckpoint.cs:39-48; SinkRoutedStageRunner not yet read for the store case).
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If the merge target runner is bound to HTTP pagination state, Phase 2 needs its own runner or a new checkpoint field; a new field changes checkpoint bytes for every YAML integration unless it is omitted when default (K3).

claim.statement: Proceeding on unverified: a from_store step with no operation can compile into StepPlan without breaking its public shape. StepPlan (engine Compile/Contracts/Models/StepPlan.cs:22-25) takes non-nullable OperationKey and OperationConfig Operation, and both schema copies require operation (integration.schema.json stage item 1572-1575, flowStep 1948-1951).
claim.consequenceIfWrong: Making Operation nullable is a breaking change to a public record (major version, every host recompiles); synthesizing a placeholder operation leaks a fake operation into plans and PlanDiffer output. The plan must choose one and record it as a decision.

claim.statement: Proceeding on unverified: the engine stage runner can learn whether a paginated walk ended by natural exhaustion or by pagination.max_pages, so a store-writing step can refuse to complete its set on a max_pages stop.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If the paginator does not surface the stop reason, guarantee 2 of D1 cannot be enforced without a paginator change, and a truncated freeze is persisted as complete (RC15).

claim.statement: Proceeding on unverified: new PlanJson/PlanDigest-visible StepPlan properties marked JsonIgnore(Condition = WhenWritingNull) leave the digest and the serialized plan of every definition that does not use them byte-identical, while the existing null properties (Topic, ForEach, MergeInto, ...) keep serializing as null.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If the attribute is not honored by SerializeToNode in PlanDigest or by PlanJson, every pinned plan fails DigestMismatch after the engine upgrade (RC10), violating K3 for integrations that never opted in.

claim.statement: Proceeding on unverified: the Falcon pilot is authored as a flow file (steps:, validated by the flowStep schema, which carries when:), and the legacy workflow stage item has no when: key (integration.schema.json 1569-1657), so the worked example needs only flowStep; the legacy stage copy still needs store/from_store to keep both authoring surfaces equal (L2).
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If the pilot is dispatched through the legacy workflow: block, the when: stored_absent guard is unavailable there and the legacy schema also needs when:.

alternative.statement: Phase 2 as a batched for_each over the stored key list, running the Spotlight operation once per key batch and publishing its records
alternative.rejectionRationale: Falcon output is the correlated host envelope (host plus findings[], zero-finding hosts kept, chunk framing). That shape exists only in merge_into (group, require_key, chunk, unmatched keep). A for_each walk publishes raw findings and loses the envelope; reading the stored set as the merge target reuses all of it.

alternative.statement: Allow a store-writing step to also carry topic or merge_into in this phase (tee records to storage and to egress)
alternative.rejectionRationale: Not needed by the Falcon freeze, doubles the runner paths to test, and K4 defers flexibility. A later phase can lift the restriction without changing any definition written under it.

alternative.statement: Change PlanDigest (or PlanJson) options globally to DefaultIgnoreCondition = WhenWritingNull so new null properties vanish from the digest
alternative.rejectionRationale: Existing null StepPlan properties (Topic, ForEach, MergeInto, Collect, When ...) serialize today as null; ignoring nulls globally changes the digest of every existing plan, which is the exact K3 violation it tries to avoid (RC10). The ignore condition belongs on the new properties only.

alternative.statement: Discover stored-set members by listing the set prefix (ListAsync) instead of reading a manifest
alternative.rejectionRationale: A crashed and restarted spool can leave stale higher-numbered parts from the first attempt; a listing would include them. Only a manifest written last, naming its parts, gives complete-or-absent (D1 guarantee 2). Listing also needs s3:ListBucket on every read (L7).

decision.statement: The D1 primitives are three YAML keys: store: {set} on a step (write the step records as a stored set: one part per page, manifest last), from_store: {set} on a step in place of operation (the step records are the set parts, one page per part, usable as a merge_into target), and two when: predicates stored_complete / stored_absent (closed named predicates, no negation). Set paths are literal (no templates), relative to the storageUrl run root, segments [A-Za-z0-9._-], first segment starts with _. Reads see only the parts the manifest names.
decision.rationale: Smallest vocabulary that writes Falcon two-phase freeze (K7) and keeps D1 guarantees checkable at load time; reuses merge_into for correlation (PALT1) and manifest-bounded reads (PALT4).

decision.statement: Failure rules: a store step whose walk ends at max_pages fails the run with a named error (never completes, never silently succeeds); a from_store read of a set with no manifest fails the run; a definition that declares any storage key fails the run when the host supplies no storage; a store step carries no topic and no merge_into in this phase (PALT2).
decision.rationale: A skipped or empty Phase 2 would publish zero findings with a success result; Falcon native fails loud on a missing store or a lost generation (RC1). D1 guarantee 2 says only never completes; failing is the stricter reading.

decision.statement: Non-opt-in identity rule: every new StepPlan property is nullable and carries JsonIgnore(Condition = WhenWritingNull); no existing property, serializer option or checkpoint field changes; the storage port is exposed from IWorkflowHost as a default member returning null; the host resolves IAdapterObjectStore only when the plan declares storage.
decision.rationale: K3/K7: definitions that do not opt in keep plan digest, PlanJson text, checkpoint bytes and published output identical, and no host is forced to require an object store (RC10, PALT3).

data.question: Which engine seams does an opt-in stored-set capability (store, from_store, stored_absent) touch, and what keeps non-opt-in plans, checkpoints and output identical?

newLessons.statement: The Falcon findings flow reaches OnTerminalSnapshotWithoutPublishedPage when a Phase 2 deferral snapshots its position without advancing the page.
newLessons.outcome: That method is declared on FalconAssetsCheckpointWriter and is called only from the ASSETS scroll runner. The findings flow never invokes it; the FalconFindingsFlow reference to it is a doc-comment cross-reference, not a call site. The conclusion it was cited for is true by a different route: the findings path's only AdvancePage is inside checkpointWriter.OnBatchPublished, which runs after a successful publish, and both throw paths escape before it.

## Durable sources read

- `cymulate-integration-adapters/docs/two-phase-correlation-and-the-object-store-capability.md` — the
  design of record across four repos. Settles: the invariant ("never place per-page enrichment inside a
  scroll filtered and sorted on a mutable field"), the measured 29.2% Falcon asset replay, layering
  (ISB S3 → Client contract → Infra `GuardedObjectStore` → collectors), the `_staging` naming rule,
  deletion-is-garbage-collection, output keys derived from geometry not counters. It also says a YAML
  descriptor was **deliberately deferred** until the C# topology was in production (section 5).
- `IntegrationServiceBus/docs/two-phase-…md` and `IntegrationInfra/docs/two-phase-…md` — pointers; the
  four host rules (multipart for unknown-length streams, prefix = path children, 403 is not absent,
  denied delete throws) and IAM grants (`s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:ListBucket`;
  `s3:DeleteObject` only with `ObjectPruningEnabled`).
- `cymulate-integration-adapters/CLAUDE.md` — YamlAdapter is the one assembly serving every YAML vendor;
  `Cymulate.IntegrationInfra` is the only Cymulate package a project may declare.
- `yaml-adapter-engine/CLAUDE.md` rule 0 and `ARCHITECTURE.md` — no `Cymulate.*` dependency; host

## What the native collectors do today (K2)

### FalconCollector — technique: two-phase freeze (`key_driven_probe`) — RC1, RC4

| step | what happens | code |
|---|---|---|
| bind | `IAdapterObjectStore` (+ optional `IAdapterObjectPruner`) from `IAdapterExecutionContext.Services`, wrapped in `GuardedObjectStore`; missing store or `storageUrl` **fails the run** (no silent fallback) | `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:758-791` |
| Phase 1 | page the Discover scroll (`last_seen_timestamp` filter/sort), write host pages only, no enrichment: `{storageUrl}/_staging/gen_<hex ticks>/hosts_NNNNNN.json`; `manifest.json` last = proof Phase 1 completed; policy edges `edges_NNNNNN.json` beside the page | `FalconStagingPaths.cs:24-205`, `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:567-628` |
| freeze | a completed generation is **reused, never re-derived**; a progressed checkpoint whose generation is gone fails | `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:578-598` |
| Phase 2 | walk the frozen aid list (`FalconFrozenKeyList.EnumerateAsync`) in `AidBatchSize` batches; one aid-scoped Spotlight scroll per batch; publish one object per batch through `NdjsonBatchEmitter` | `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:288-379` |
| resume | position is (staged page, batch index) inside one generation; object name = host page counter | `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:175-199,311-322` |
| cleanup | never deletes a completed generation (checkpoint write has no durable ack); run-scoped lifecycle reclaims | `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:376-418` |

**Result:** stability comes from the freeze, not from storage (RC4). S3 is where the frozen list and
the staged pages survive across legs and pods.

### TenableIoCollector — technique: keyed asset spine (`grouped_probe`-like) — RC2

- Spool `/assets/export` to `_staging/spine/<assetId>.json` (one object per asset, identity key, so a
  re-spool converges); spine manifest through Infra `StagingManifest`.
- Stream `/vulns/export` chunks; look each asset up by key (`TryReadAsync` → null = miss).
- Claim marker per published chunk `_staging/claims/<chunkId>.ids`, written **before** the data object.
- Sweep assets no chunk claimed as empty-findings envelopes; delete spine if a pruner exists.
- Purpose: bounded heap and resume-safe correlation of two independently snapshotted exports. Not a
  mutable-scroll freeze.
- Code: `TenableIoAssetSpine.cs:13-404`, `TenableIoSpinePaths.cs:5-74`, `TenableIoCorrelatedFindingsFlow.cs:14-335`.

### Which IntegrationInfra primitives are really used — RC3 (C1 rejected)

| primitive | used by | status |
|---|---|---|
| `GuardedObjectStore` | Falcon, Tenable.io | exercised |
| `StagingManifest` | Tenable.io only | exercised |
| `BatchScopedStorage.ResolveBaseUrl` | Falcon, Tenable.io (base storage URL) | exercised |
| `FrozenKeyList` | nobody (Falcon has its own `FalconFrozenKeyList`) | **unexercised** |
| `PriorStateStore` | nobody (Tenable remarks explain why not) | **unexercised** |

C1 was rejected because it named `FrozenKeyList`/`PriorStateStore` as in use and attributed Tenable's
use to inventory stability. RC1–RC4 replace it.

| adapters `YamlAdapter/.../Sinks/WorkflowPublishSink.cs` | egress; unchanged | adapters reference |
| adapters `YamlAdapter/.../Recovery/StageCheckpointWriter.cs`, `YamlCollectorCheckpointState.cs` | checkpoint write | adapters work if the position gains fields |

## Patterns to mirror

- Host port with default members → `IWorkflowHost.cs:72,79` (`StepStarted`/`StepCompleted` default
  no-ops so every existing host compiles untouched).
- Resolve storage from DI, never construct a client; fail hard when required and absent →
  `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:758-791`, `TenableIoAssetSpine.cs:120-125`.
- Always go through `GuardedObjectStore` with `IngestionOptions.Resolve` / `MemoryPressureOptions.Resolve`
  → `TenableIoCorrelatedFindingsFlow.cs:326-330`.
- Base URL from `BatchScopedStorage.ResolveBaseUrl`, never re-implemented → `BatchScopedStorage.cs:207-218`.
- Staged paths under `_staging/`, asserted at run start → `FalconStagingPaths.cs:120-156`.
- Write-once frozen list; completion proved by a manifest written last; reuse, never re-derive →
  `FalconFindingsFlow.cs:557-628`; design doc section 5.
- Deterministic keys from identity or geometry, never a counter → design doc section 6.
- Checkpoint: `SetState` before `AdvancePage` → `StageCheckpointWriter.cs:9-16`.
- Opt-in by absence: a stage feature exists only when its key is present (e.g. `merge_into`, `collect`,
  `poll` are nullable on `StageConfig`/`StepPlan`).

## Existing engine mechanism the design must extend, not duplicate — RC8, RC14

- `collect:` on a stage accumulates distinct values in first-appearance order
  (`StageCollections.cs:7-62`); a later `for_each: "{{stages.X.collected.k}}"` stage runs once per
  element (`FanOutStageRunner.cs:23-58,114-133`); resume is positional (`ForEachIndex`).
- That **is** a two-phase freeze — but the list lives only in heap and in `WorkflowCheckpoint.StagesOutputJson`,
  re-serialized into the ISB checkpoint row on every page and item (`StageCheckpointWriter.cs:47-61`).
- Lesson L-35b88c57 (applied as RC14, OPEN): nothing caps that blob; a native sibling measured 460,022
  bytes for 5,000 keys. The S3-backed list is the bounded alternative.
- `for_each` runs one operation per element; Falcon needs one call per **batch** of keys
  (`aid:[…]`, 50 native / 250 YAML). Batching over a frozen list does not exist in `for_each` today
  (read of `FanOutStageRunner.ResolveItems`; not exhaustively searched for a chunking transform).

## The pilot today — RC7, C4

- `integration-yaml` master Falcon `collect` flow: `hosts` stage scrolls Discover
  (`filter last_seen_timestamp:>=`, `sort last_seen_timestamp.asc`, page 250, prefetch) and the
  `findings` stage is `merge_into: target: hosts` — Spotlight enrichment **per page inside the scroll**
  (`SinkRoutedStageRunner.cs:5-17`, `MergeEnrichmentSink.cs:13-22`).
- That is exactly the shape the design of record measured at 29.2% replay. Parity target is native
  v5.0.0, which predates two-phase.
- C4 stays OPEN: the definition uses only supported constructs and its native counterpart uses S3
  (RE14), but no deployment record was read, so "runs in production today" is not established.

## Shared surface to freeze

- **Engine storage port** (new, engine-owned, public): the minimal read/write/stat/list the engine needs
  over a run-scoped relative path, with absence as a value. Produced by engine work; consumed by the
  YamlAdapter host. Shape is a design decision for the contract/plan, not settled here.
- **How the host exposes it**: a new member on `IWorkflowHost` with a default body, or a separate
  interface the host may also implement (the `IResumeStateSink` precedent). Decide once, before either
  side starts.
- **YAML vocabulary**: key name(s), where they attach (flow step and legacy workflow stage are two
  separate schema copies — `flowStep` 1945-2042 and stage item 1569-1657), validation rules.
- **Staged layout contract**: `_staging/<something>/…`, manifest-last, deterministic order (RC16).
- **StepPlan field(s)** and their digest behaviour when absent (L3).

## Disjoint sets available

- `engine`: `yaml-adapter-engine/src/**` + `tests/**` — independent of `host` once the port is frozen.
- `host`: `cymulate-integration-adapters/src/Cymulate.Integration.Adapters/YamlAdapter/**` + its test
  project + `Directory.Packages.props` pin — depends on a **published** engine package carrying the port.
- `pilot`: `integration-yaml/integrations/crowdstrike-falcon/**` — depends on an engine release and an
  adapters release; K4 puts integration-specific use later.
- Split is by repository, so the multi-repo hard trigger applies. Engine tests and engine src are
  separable within `engine`.

## Landmines

- **L1 — IntegrationInfra origin/dev is not what runs.** Adapters pin `Cymulate.IntegrationInfra
  1.8.0-preview.0`; Infra origin/dev is `1.2.0-preview.0` (2026-08-16); newest line is
  `origin/refactor/appcore-namespaces` `1.10.0-preview.0`. The object-store surface is byte-identical
  across them (RC11), so this does not change the design — but no one should "fix" Infra dev as part
  of this task. Remote fetch was denied by the sandbox; refs are as last fetched.
- **L2 — The schema is closed.** `additionalProperties: false` at root (line 7), workflow (1560), stage
  item (1571), mergeInto (1700), flowStep (1947). A new key needs an engine release before any
  definition can carry it, and a definition carrying it fails `INVALID_PAYLOAD` on an older engine pin.
  Two schema copies (flowStep and workflow stage) must both change or the key works on one authoring
  surface only. Definitions deployed to S3 drift per environment (`YamlEngineFactory.cs:23-30`).
- **L3 — Plan digest changes for everyone.** `PlanDigest` serializes nulls, so any new `StepPlan`
  property changes every plan's digest; a pinned plan digested by an older engine then falls back with
  `DigestMismatch` logged at Error for integrations that never declared the capability — a K3
  violation unless the new property is omitted when absent (RC10, OPEN, needs a test). The plan
  producer is outside ISB (no `PlanDigest` reference there).
- **L4 — Parser visibility.** YAML egress writes `assets_*`/`findings_*` at the run root. Staged
  objects must sit under a leading-underscore segment (RC13); mirror the native run-start assertion.
- **L5 — Read-slot deadlock.** `GuardedObjectStore` enumerators (`ListAsync`, NDJSON reads) take no
  slot by design; a host adapter that wraps them must not hold a slot across a `yield` into engine code
  (Infra doc rule 2). At `MaxConcurrentReads: 1` it deadlocks.
- **L6 — Unknown-length writes.** A streamed staged list must reach S3 through multipart; ISB
  `S3ObjectStore` already does this for non-seekable streams. A host that buffers instead gives up the
  bounded-memory property.
- **L7 — IAM.** `s3:ListBucket` is required or `StatAsync` throws access-denied rather than returning
  absent. Deployment-time, not checkable from here.
- **L8 — Resume authority.** Falcon refuses to derive a second "where are we" from storage; the
  checkpoint is the only position authority and a manifest proves only completion. The YAML design
  must keep one authority (the `WorkflowCheckpoint`) and treat the manifest as a completion proof.
- **L9 — Truncated freeze.** `expected_total_path` does not fire on a `max_pages` stop (lesson GC1,
  applied as RC15, OPEN). A freeze over a capped walk would persist a short list as complete and every
  later leg reuses it.
- **L10 — Deterministic order.** Batch k must cover the same keys on every leg; the persisted list's
  order must be contractual, never a `Dictionary`/`HashSet` enumeration (lesson L-1a37307e, RC16, OPEN).
- **L11 — Local YamlCollector remnants.** `Collectors/YamlCollector/Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine`
  exists only as untracked build output locally; it is a vendored engine copy that must never load
  beside YamlAdapter (adapters CLAUDE.md). Ignore it.
- **L12 — Design-of-record tension.** The design doc deferred a YAML descriptor on purpose ("a second
  declarative interpreter beside the existing engine is a known trap"). This task adds the capability to
  the existing engine rather than a second interpreter, which is consistent with that warning, but the
  contract should say so.

## Lesson applicability

| lesson | decision | reason |
|---|---|---|
| L-35b88c57 (checkpoint key list has no ceiling) | applied → RC14 | the engine's existing collect/for_each keeps the list in checkpoint state |
| GC1 (expected_total_path skips max_pages stop) | applied → RC15 | a freeze must be provably complete |
| L-1a37307e (do not rely on Dictionary order for a persisted artifact) | applied → RC16 | positional frozen list |
| GC2 (cursor must be a JSON string) | not applied | Falcon `meta.pagination.after` is a string; not a storage concern |
| L-76ed5c8b (404 under 200 on cursor expiry) | not applied | Phase-1 scroll recovery, pilot-specific; K4 defers pilot use |
| L-29828585 (AID derivation for unmanaged hosts) | not applied | pilot key extraction, not the storage capability |
| L-cc8f607b (two lanes on different vendor clocks) | not applied | pilot correlation semantics, later phase |
| L-f88b5876 (lab re-collection cost) | not applied as a claim; noted for verification planning | live Falcon runs are expensive and not repeatable at will |
| L-00f62476 (settings_hash presence) | not applied | vendor field, unrelated |
| ALT2 Axonius v1 | not applied | unrelated vendor |

## Claims and disposition

| claim | status | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | rejected | RE3 |
| C2 | rejected | RE5 |
| C3 | open (structurally supported by RE9; blocked on L3) | RE9 |
| C4 | open (production dispatch not established) | RE14 |
| RC1–RC9, RC11–RC13 | validated | RE1–RE9, RE11–RE13 |
| RC10 | open — needs a test | RE10 |
| RC14–RC16 | open — lesson-derived | — |

Discarded approaches: RALT1 (engine references Client/AWSSDK), RALT2 (host uses YamlAdapter's own
AWSSDK.S3 client).

## What recon leaves to the contract and plan

- Whether the capability is (a) a generic staged read/write port only, or (b) the port plus a declared
  "freeze-then-walk" topology over it (Falcon's shape). K2/K3/K4 read as (b) for Falcon being the pilot;
  confirm in the contract.
- Whether batching over a frozen list is new engine vocabulary or an extension of `for_each`.
- Release order: engine publish → adapters pin bump + host port → definition change.

Revision 2 answers the first two: D1 chose option C (no fixed topology); PD1 composes the freeze from
`store` / `from_store` / `stored_absent`, and Phase 2 reuses `merge_into` rather than batching
`for_each` (PALT1).

## Revision 2 — contract-design findings

Run `RD1`, engine read at the dev checkout (seam files identical on master, RC12).

### Seams read for the contract

| file | finding | used for |
|---|---|---|

| engine `Workflow/Contracts/Models/WhenConfig.cs:29-46` | closed predicates `input_set`, `not_empty`; exactly one; no negation by design | `stored_absent` / `stored_complete` as two more named predicates |

artifact.content:
# Prompt Contract — YAML engine reads and writes the ISB-provided S3 storage

Role:
You are a senior .NET engineer working across `yaml-adapter-engine` and
`cymulate-integration-adapters` (YamlAdapter). You add an opt-in storage capability to the engine and
its host. You do not change ISB or IntegrationInfra.

Goal:
A YAML definition can write the records of a step into the run's S3 storage (`storageUrl`) as a
**stored set**, check whether a complete set exists, and read a stored set back as the record source
of a later step. Composed in the YAML, this reproduces Falcon's native two-phase freeze. A definition
that does not declare the capability behaves exactly as today.

Context:
- Recon: current InternalRecon artifact (research/internal-recon.md). Read it before planning.
- What the native collectors do (RC1, RC2, RC4): Falcon spools the Discover scroll to
  `_staging/gen_<ticks>/hosts_NNNNNN.json`, writes `manifest.json` last, reuses a completed
  generation and never re-derives it, then walks the frozen aid list in batches for Spotlight.
  Stability comes from the freeze; S3 is where the frozen list survives across legs and pods.
- Access path (RC5, RC6): ISB registers `IAdapterObjectStore` in `IAdapterExecutionContext.Services`
  when a data bucket is configured. YamlAdapter does not resolve it today. The engine may not
  reference any `Cymulate.*` package, so the engine owns a storage port and YamlAdapter implements it.
- The engine already has an in-memory two-phase shape (`collect:` then `for_each`, RC8). Its list
  lives in checkpoint state with no size ceiling (RC14). The stored set is the bounded alternative.
- The Falcon YAML pilot enriches inside the mutable scroll (RC7), the shape measured at 29.2% replay.
- Governing decisions: D1 (option C with four guarantees), PD1 (vocabulary), PD2 (failure rules),
  PD3 (non-opt-in identity). Rejected: ALT1, ALT2, RALT1, RALT2, PALT1 to PALT4.

## The capability (PD1)

Three additions to a step. Both schema copies change: `flowStep` and the legacy workflow stage item.

| key | where | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `store: { set: <path> }` | step with `operation`, no `topic`, no `merge_into` | the step's mapped records are written as the set: one part per page, in page order, records in response order; the manifest is written last and only after natural exhaustion of the walk |
| `from_store: { set: <path> }` | step **instead of** `operation` | the step's records are the set's parts, one page per part, in manifest order; the step may carry `topic`, `counts` and may be a `merge_into` target |
| `when: { stored_complete: <path> }` / `when: { stored_absent: <path> }` | any step with `when` | closed named predicates; `stored_absent` is true when no manifest exists (a partial set counts as absent) |

Path rules, checked at load time: literal string, no template; relative to the run root from
`BatchScopedStorage.ResolveBaseUrl`; segments separated by `/`, each non-empty, characters
`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, no `.` or `..` segment; the **first segment starts with `_`** (RC13, ALT2).
A `from_store` set must be written by an earlier `store` step in the same flow; the compiler derives
the dependency edge from it.

Physical layout (the plan fixes the exact names): `<path>/part_NNNNNN.<ext>` and `<path>/manifest.json`.
The manifest names its parts and record counts. Reads and predicates use only the manifest, never a
prefix listing (PALT4). Deletion is out of scope: the run-scoped lifecycle reclaims (native rule).

## Worked example — Falcon two-phase freeze with only these primitives (K7)

Written against `integration-yaml` origin/master `72a99e2`, `integrations/crowdstrike-falcon/flows/collect.yaml`.
Operations are unchanged. Not deployed in this phase (K4).

```yaml
capability: collector
steps:
  - name: assets
    operation: get_devices
    topic: assets

  # Phase 1 — page the Discover scroll, store host records only, no enrichment.
  # Skipped when a complete set already exists (a leg that crashed after the manifest was
  # written but before the checkpoint moved on): the freeze is reused, never re-derived.
  - name: hosts_freeze
    operation: query_hosts_for_findings
    store:
      set: "_falcon/hosts"
    when:
      stored_absent: "_falcon/hosts"

  # Phase 2 — walk the frozen set. One stored part (250 hosts) per page.
  - name: hosts
    from_store:
      set: "_falcon/hosts"
    topic: findings
    counts:
      findings: "findings[]"

  - name: findings
    operation: get_findings_for_hosts
    merge_into:
      target: hosts
      # on, as, group, require_key, strip, sort, chunk, unmatched, unmatched_value:
      # unchanged from 72a99e2
      batch_size: 250
```

Design-level validation against the engine (aabc8cf / fa10015):

| element | engine today | what changes | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `store`, `from_store` keys | `flowStep` is closed (`additionalProperties: false`, RC9) | schema adds both keys to both copies | needs engine change |
| `hosts` step without `operation` | both schema copies require `operation`; `StepPlan` requires `OperationKey` and `Operation` | schema: exactly one of `operation` / `from_store`; StepPlan representation open (PC3) | **open design item** |
| `when: stored_absent` | `WhenConfig` has `input_set`, `not_empty` (closed, one predicate) | two more named predicates | needs engine change |
| `merge_into: target: hosts` on a `from_store` step | enrichment runs per page of the target (`SinkRoutedStageRunner`) | the target pages come from parts; resume by `InTargetStage` + `TargetPage` (PC2) | **open design item** |
| truncated freeze | `expected_total_path` skips a `max_pages` stop (RC15) | store step fails the run on a `max_pages` stop (PD2); requires the stop reason (PC4) | **open design item** |
| deterministic order | `collect:` is first-appearance order | parts in page order, records in response order, read in manifest order (RC16) | needs engine change |
| parser visibility | egress writes `assets_*`/`findings_*` at the run root | `_falcon/...` is invisible to the undelimited prefix match (RC13) | satisfied by path rule |
| run scoping | fixed path within `storageUrl` | correct only if `storageUrl` is per run (PC1) | **open assumption** |

Result: the freeze **can be written** with D1 primitives. No primitive is missing, provided PC1 holds.
If PC1 is false, the missing primitive is a per-run generation token recorded in `WorkflowCheckpoint`.

Differences from native, accepted for this phase: part size equals the Phase-1 page size (250), not
native `AidBatchSize` 50; policy edges (`edges_NNNNNN.json`) are not reproduced.

## How integrations that do not opt in stay identical (K3, K7, PD3)

- New `StepPlan` properties are nullable with `JsonIgnore(Condition = WhenWritingNull)` on each new
  property only. Serializer options stay as they are (PALT3). PlanDigest and PlanJson text of every
  existing definition are unchanged (RC10, PC5).
- No `WorkflowCheckpoint` property is added unless it is omitted when default; reuse of
  `TargetPage` is preferred (PC2).
- The storage port is reached through a new `IWorkflowHost` member with a default body returning
  `null`. Existing hosts compile untouched (pattern: `IWorkflowHost.cs:72,79`).
- YamlAdapter resolves `IAdapterObjectStore` only when the compiled plan declares storage. A run that
  does not declare it never touches the object store, needs no bucket and no IAM change.
- Existing stage runners are unchanged for steps without the new keys.

Constraints:
- K1 source of truth: engine origin/master compared with origin/dev (master is a strict ancestor,
  RC12); adapters, ISB, Infra at origin/dev. Engine branches follow the repository flow (dev, then master).
- No change to IntegrationServiceBus or IntegrationInfra (RC5, RC11). Do not "fix" Infra dev (L1).
- Engine: no `Cymulate.*` or AWS SDK reference (RC6, RALT1). The port is engine-owned and public;
  it is a minor-version addition.
- Host: storage only through `IAdapterObjectStore` from `context.Services`, wrapped in
  `GuardedObjectStore`, base URL from `BatchScopedStorage.ResolveBaseUrl` (RALT2). Never hold a read
  slot across a `yield` into engine code (L5). Unknown-length writes stream (L6).
- The `WorkflowCheckpoint` stays the only resume-position authority; a manifest proves completion only (L8).
- Failure rules PD2 apply. No silent fallback, no empty-success Phase 2.
- Both schema copies change together (L2). `tools/.../LocalRunner` is checked for engine internals it
  reimplements.
- No deletion, no pruner use, no path templating, no store-plus-topic tee in this phase (K4, PALT2).
- The pilot definition in `integration-yaml` is not changed or deployed in this phase (K4).
- Release order: engine package, then adapters pin bump with the host implementation.
- Identifier prefixes per K6.

Success Criteria:
1. Engine schema accepts the worked example; a definition with a first segment not starting with
   `_`, a template in a path, a `..` segment, `store` together with `topic` or `merge_into`,
   `from_store` together with `operation`, or `from_store` of a set no earlier step stores, is
   refused at load time with a named error.
2. The worked example is an engine test fixture that loads with schema validation, compiles, and runs
   against an in-memory storage port and stub HTTP. The test shows: Phase 1 writes parts and the
   manifest last; Phase 2 publishes the correlated envelopes from the stored parts; a re-run with a
   complete set skips Phase 1 and issues no Discover request.
3. Resume: a crash inside Phase 2 resumes at the next part with no re-fetch of completed parts and
   no duplicate publication; a crash after the manifest but before the checkpoint skips Phase 1.
4. A store step stopped by `max_pages` fails the run and leaves no manifest. A `from_store` read with
   no manifest fails the run. A definition declaring storage fails the run when the host returns no
   storage.
5. Stale parts from a crashed first spool beyond the manifest's part count are never read.
6. Identity: for every existing definition fixture in the engine test suite, PlanDigest and PlanJson
   text are byte-identical before and after the change (a test compares against digests produced
   by the unchanged engine). The existing engine and YamlAdapter suites pass unchanged.
7. YamlAdapter implements the port over `GuardedObjectStore`; a host test shows it resolves the
   object store only for a plan that declares storage, writes under the run root, and refuses a
   path whose first segment does not start with `_`.
8. PC1 to PC6 and RC10, RC14, RC15, RC16 each carry a verifier disposition with a citation.

Execution Rules:
- Do not assume missing data. Resolve PC1 from source or escalate before relying on fixed paths.
- Respect constraints strictly. A worker needing a shared artifact not frozen in phase 0 returns `BLOCKED:`.
- Record new claims, evidence and decisions in the ledger, not in notes.

Output Format:
- Engine: schema, model, compiler, runner, port, validators and tests on an engine branch.
- Adapters: YamlAdapter port implementation, pin bump and tests on an adapters branch.
- `execution_notes.md` in the task directory; verifier and code-reviewer outputs under `review/`.

Stop Conditions:
- When every success criterion is met and verified.
- When PC1 is refuted: stop, the generation-token primitive is a design change back to Design.
- When PC3 or PC2 forces a breaking public change or a new checkpoint field that alters bytes for
  non-opt-in definitions: stop and return to Design.
- When required data is missing, or a change would touch ISB, IntegrationInfra or `integration-yaml`.

claim.statement: IAdapterObjectStore offers four operations and no delete: StatAsync (null = absent; the existence and resume primitive), OpenReadAsync (non-nullable stream, absence throws ObjectNotFoundException), WriteAsync (replace-on-write, all-or-nothing per object, forward-only unknown-length streams go through a multipart upload, ETag null on that path) and ListAsync (lazy, path-separator-bounded prefix, store key order only). There is no conditional write and no multi-object atomicity, so a manifest written last is the only way to mark a multi-object set complete. Deletion is a separate IAdapterObjectPruner, registered only when ObjectPruningEnabled is true.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: A design that relies on atomic multi-object writes, compare-and-set, list order or ETag as a content hash would be wrong on the real store.

claim.statement: Native Falcon Phase 1 (FalconHostSpooler.SpoolAsync) has no page-count stop. It follows the Discover after-token until the vendor terminal (after absent or empty string, normalised to null). It re-anchors in-process, never stops, in three cases: (a) proactively after MaxPagesPerCursorScroll pages on one cursor (default 500, clamp 1..100000), only when the page still has an after-token AND at least one fresh host carries last_seen; the stated reason is that server-side scroll context degrades with depth (hard 500 near page 1542), not cursor ageing; (b) FalconCursorExpiredException (404 on an after request; after-token TTL 120s); (c) HTTP status >= 500, up to 5 consecutive (counter resets on any good page), after which the exception escapes and the host defers. A re-anchor issues a new query filtered last_seen_timestamp:>= the watermark (whole second) or the base-date floor, with after=null, and resets the per-cursor page counter. The only other exits are 5 consecutive empty pages that still carry an after-token (truncation, see FTC6) and cancellation.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: A YAML Phase-1 walk bounded by pagination.max_pages, or one without a re-anchor, cannot reproduce the native walk on large tenants.

claim.statement: Store failures reach a caller only as ObjectStoreException subtypes: 404 is null from StatAsync and ObjectNotFoundException from OpenReadAsync; 403/401 is ObjectStoreAccessDeniedException (never retry; a 403 on HEAD is never reported as absent); 5xx, 408, 429, SlowDown, RequestTimeout and an inner HttpRequestException or TaskCanceledException are ObjectStoreTransientException; any other 4xx and a missing data-bucket configuration are the base ObjectStoreException; cancellation is an unwrapped OperationCanceledException. Neither S3ObjectStore nor GuardedObjectStore retries; the caller owns retry, and only Transient is retryable. GuardedObjectStore limit breaches are DataPipelineException, outside this hierarchy.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: An engine port that collapses these into one failure, retries AccessDenied, or treats a limit breach as a store fault would either loop forever or misreport a lost set.

claim.statement: Native Phase 1 dedup has two layers, both held for the whole spool and never reset by a re-anchor. (1) Boundary set: record keys of staged hosts whose last_seen falls in the watermark second; cleared when the watermark advances; capped at 5000 (MaxBoundaryAids); a host re-served at that second is dropped before staging. (2) Run-wide key claim: Dictionary of record key -> 32-bit hash of the Discover combined id. Same key and same identity = benign replay, dropped silently. Same key and different identity = collision: the host is NOT staged, is logged at Error, and is counted into the freeze ledger unresolved counter. Freshness guard: only hosts passing both layers are staged; the watermark advances only from staged hosts (page max, truncated to the second, monotonic because the sort is last_seen.asc); a page of only duplicates still reports a heartbeat. The staged key list therefore has first-appearance order and no duplicates.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: A YAML freeze without key-level dedup stages a re-served host twice after every re-anchor; one without identity comparison cannot tell replay from key collision.

claim.statement: Native staged page layout: key {storageUrl run root}/_staging/gen_<16 hex UTC ticks>/hosts_NNNNNN.json, where NNNNNN is the spool page index restarting at 0 for each generation (positional, never a counter across attempts). Content is NDJSON, one line per host: {aid, sensorAid, lastSeen, host: verbatim Discover record}, property order preserved. One vendor page may become several staged objects: fresh hosts are chunked to at most hostsPerPage (the requested Discover limit, default 1000), so a staged object never exceeds the manifest stride; vendor fill is below the request (229-969 of 1000 observed). A page with no fresh host writes no object. Pages are written through GuardedObjectStore.WriteAsync from a fully buffered MemoryStream (stream form avoids the 8 MiB in-memory refusal, not the buffering). Staged host pages are immutable once the manifest exists.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: A YAML stored set whose part boundaries follow vendor page fill is not the native geometry; if part size must be bounded, parts need re-chunking.

claim.statement: Path handling in the contract is weaker than the PD1 path rule. The bucket always comes from configuration (DataBucket / DataBucketUrl), never from the path, and a scheme and bucket in the path are discarded; the key is the optional data prefix plus the path. ObjectLocation rejects only a '..' segment and control characters, and collapses empty segments. It accepts a '.' segment, spaces, backslashes and any other character, and it does not require a leading underscore. PD1's rules (segments [A-Za-z0-9._-], no '.' or '..', first segment starts with '_') must therefore be enforced by the engine at load time and again by the host port. The contract does not enforce them.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: A design that treats ObjectLocation validation as the parser-visibility guard would let a path such as 'assets_x/part' through to the run root, where the parser ingests it as customer data (RC13).

claim.statement: The native manifest (_staging/gen_<id>/manifest.json) is written FIRST, immediately after the last Discover page and before any policy work, and is rewritten after each later stage, each time only after that stage's own objects have landed. It carries generationId, createdUtc, hostCount, hostsPerPage, aidBatchSize, pageKeys (the ordered staged page paths: this list IS the frozen key list), the Discover watermark and up to 5000 watermark keys, ledgerVersion, three O(1) stage ledger lines (hostFreeze, policyFetch, policyEdges) and policyGenerationId. It is written buffered and read back with GuardedObjectStore.ReadAllBytesAsync under IngestionOptions.MaxControlArtifactBytes (1 MiB default). Over that ceiling the read throws and the run FAILS (no re-spool, since a re-spool would write an equally large manifest); pageKeys cost about 48 bytes per staged page and a Warning fires at 75 percent. A manifest that is absent, unparseable, from a newer ledgerVersion, or missing generationId/hostsPerPage/aidBatchSize/pageKeys is treated as absent and Phase 1 re-spools (present-but-unusable is logged at Warning).
claim.consequenceIfWrong: A YAML stored-set manifest that names every part and is read through the same guarded control-artifact path inherits the 1 MiB ceiling, so set size is bounded by part count unless parts are large or the manifest is streamed.

claim.statement: The native manifest proves only that the Discover scroll ended, not that it was complete. When the spool stops with a live after-token (more than 5 consecutive empty pages), it logs at Error, still writes the manifest, and records the freeze as Degraded (units = stagedPages + 1). Key collisions are recorded as unresolved and do not change the state. No caller reads the freeze state: a degraded freeze is reused like a complete one, Phase 2 publishes from it, and the run returns success. Native Falcon therefore does not fail a truncated freeze. PD2's rule (a store step that ends at max_pages fails the run) is stricter than native.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: Whoever copies native behaviour literally keeps the silent-success path; PD2 should be recorded as a deliberate difference from native, not as parity.

claim.statement: Lifecycle, pruning and IAM. Deletion is garbage collection and never a progress marker.
