claim.statement: Native generation selection (FalconFindingsFlow.ResolveFrozenKeyListAsync), in order: (1) if the checkpoint names a StagingGenerationId, read that manifest by fixed key; if it is gone and the checkpoint has a position (page or batch >= 0), FAIL; (2) otherwise list _staging/ with ListAsync and adopt the newest generation whose manifest exists (lexical max of the fixed-width tick id), even one no checkpoint names (crash after freeze, before the first batch checkpoint); (3) otherwise mint a new generation id from UtcNow, garbage-collect every other host generation (only with a pruner; failures are logged and ignored), and spool from page one. There is no partial-freeze resume: a crash during the spool discards that attempt. Generation discovery therefore depends on prefix listing (s3:ListBucket) and on the listing returning paths relative to the run base.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: The YAML design reads a set by fixed path and never lists; that matches step (1) and is simpler, but it relies on PC1 for isolation and has no step (2) or GC of abandoned attempts; a crashed spool leaves stale parts that only the manifest bound hides (PALT4).

claim.statement: Native Phase 2 (FalconFrozenKeyList.EnumerateAsync) walks manifest.pageKeys in order. A page before the resume page is skipped without a read. For every other page it checks existence: absent at or before the resume page is skipped (legacy GC), absent after it FAILS. It reads the page (read slot released before yielding), attaches the policy envelope, then chunks the page's hosts by the MANIFEST aidBatchSize (a differing configured value only logs a Warning) and yields (pageIndex, batchIndex, hosts), skipping batchIndex <= LastCompletedBatchIndex on the resume page. So the unit of Phase 2 work, publish and checkpoint is an aid batch, a sub-division of a staged page, not the page. Each batch runs one Spotlight scroll filtered suppression_info.is_suppressed:!true, status open/reopen/closed, aid:[sensor AIDs], updated_timestamp >= base date, sorted updated_timestamp.asc; on a 404 cursor expiry it re-anchors from the last updated_timestamp and drops overlap with a per-batch seen-finding-id set; it ends only when after is null. Findings are grouped per sensor AID, a chunk record flushes at ChunkFindingsCap (2000), and every host gets a terminal isLastChunk record, zero-finding hosts included. Up to MaxConcurrentSpotlightBatches scrolls (default 6, clamp 1..16) are fetched ahead; one consumer publishes and checkpoints in frozen order.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: A YAML Phase 2 whose part equals a staged page publishes one object per page (about 1000 hosts natively) instead of per aid batch (8 hosts); object size and the Spotlight aid:[...] list length change accordingly.

claim.statement: Native resume policy: the only position authority is the checkpoint blob (format v4): stagingGenerationId plus (lastCompletedStagedPage, lastCompletedBatchIndex), -1/-1 meaning nothing published; an absent key parses as -1, never 0. The published object name is the host page counter (progressContext.CurrentPage), never derived from the position. Publish and CommitPage run as one synchronous step with nothing awaitable between them, so no object exists without the position that covers it. The collector never derives a position from storage (a helper that did was deleted); the manifest proves only stage completion. No staged object is deleted after freeze, because the host checkpoint write has no durable acknowledgement; the run-scoped lifecycle reclaims. A co-operative stop writes a StateSnapshot checkpoint without AdvancePage; batches fetched but not published are discarded and redone. Each commit also carries diagnostic fields: Discover watermark and up to 5000 watermark keys, totals. Resume is declined for a format version other than 4 or a checkpoint older than about 23 hours with no progress.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: The YAML design must keep WorkflowCheckpoint as the single position authority and treat the manifest as a completion proof only (L8); a part-index position must advance in the same step as the publish.

claim.statement: Native Falcon findings fails the run (never falls back to single-phase, never skips) on: no storageUrl; no IAdapterObjectStore (a missing pruner only skips GC with a Warning); a staging folder name that starts with assets or findings (asserted at construction); a checkpoint generation whose manifest is gone while the checkpoint has a position; a leg with no resume state that finds a completed generation AND at least one findings_*.json already published under the run root (counted by listing the run root, staging excluded) - the orphaned-leg guard; a policy contract mismatch or pre-ledger generation after anything was published or checkpointed; Phase 2 entered with the edge stage not traversed; a staged page missing ahead of the position; an edge page missing while the ledger says traversed; a malformed staged line; a manifest over the 1 MiB read ceiling. A Phase 2 transport failure outside the Spotlight scroll (staged-page read or publish) is re-thrown as FalconTransportFailureException, without an inner exception, so it defers for 5 minutes instead of failing terminally. A Spotlight scroll drop is retried in-process (3 retries, 2s base, x3 backoff, 30s per-attempt and 5 min total caps) before deferring. Migration: checkpoint format other than v4 is declined (restart when nothing published, fail when published, per 03-current-concerns.md); a pre-ledger manifest is migrated (freeze taken as complete, policy stages pending).
claim.consequenceIfWrong: PD2 covers missing storage, missing manifest and max_pages. It has no equivalent of the orphaned-leg guard (fresh leg over a run that already published) or of the transport re-throw for storage reads mid-Phase 2.

claim.statement: After the freeze, native Falcon runs a post-freeze policy stage that is a second, different use of storage. For each staged page it writes _staging/gen_<id>/edges_NNNNNN.json (NDJSON, one line per sensor AID, written for every page including an empty one) and resumes inside the stage by OBJECT EXISTENCE: a page whose edge object exists is counted and skipped. Definitions go to _staging/policies/pgen_<ticks>/definitions.json, which outlives a host re-spool and is adopted by later legs of the same run. The manifest ledger is rewritten last. Phase 2 composes each host envelope from the edge page and the definitions at read time. This existence-as-done-marker pattern is the one place native uses storage, not the checkpoint, to locate work, and it is bounded to a stage whose units are keyed deterministically.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If the D1 primitives are expected to express the policy plane later, they need a per-unit existence check or keyed write; PD1 has neither. K4 may put the policy plane out of scope for this phase; synthesis should say so explicitly.
